preceding_agent.observed_effect: The cost test did not simply measure cost robustness; its turnover and drag accounting exposed that the campaign's only positive candidate is not a momentum signal. A rule documented as rebalancing a constant-dollar +/-1 position every bar should turn over on the order of 100x capital per year; the recorded implementation turned over 3.8x per year and showed a cost drag of at most 0.001 per 84-day fold, which is only possible if the position is essentially static. The integrity audit confirmed the cause: the weight is a function of the adjusted price level, constant +1.0 in 27/30 (asset, lookback) cells, so the lookback parameter is inert and the recorded medians (+0.0686 per fold, about 20 percent a year) are the large-cap equity risk premium of a constant long position, not a short-horizon autocorrelation effect. The predeclared corrected-signal diagnostic then showed 0/30 EDGE cells at zero cost, i.e. no REGIME_STABLE positive edge even before costs. The information gain came from the accounting audit rather than from the cost grid itself: a turnover-versus-documentation plausibility check would have caught this at the first momentum cell closure, which is the process improvement recorded as a candidate task.
preceding_agent.question: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?
preceding_agent.research_result: NEGATIVE / INVALIDATING. The assigned cost grid was executed as predeclared and independently verified. For the signal as recorded (bt.momentum_signals), costs are immaterial: zero-cost 17/30 EDGE cells, realistic 18/30, stress_2x 18/30, median of cell medians unchanged at +0.0686 per 84-day fold, per-asset cost drag <= 0.001 per fold, classification 6 COST_ROBUST / 4 NO_EDGE_ZERO_COST. That result is not evidence about momentum: the audited signal is a step function of the adjusted price level (constant +1.0 in 27/30 cells; NVDA flips sign once when its split-adjusted price crosses 1.0), so the tested position is constant-long large-cap equity and the measured medians are the equity risk premium, and the lookback parameter only shifts the entry by a few bars. A docstring-faithful log-return momentum, evaluated on the identical grid with the identical rule, yields 0/30 EDGE cells at every cost level (zero-cost median of cell medians +0.0069, realistic +0.0010, stress_2x +0.0008; all 10 assets NO_EDGE_ZERO_COST) and turns over about 105x capital per year at the realistic level. No claim of profitability is made for any asset; the durable contribution is that the campaign's only positive candidate is invalidated at the implementation level, that the falsified reversal cell is likewise a constant-short position, and that the cost question is closed for this construction.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: Reduced the uncertainty from 'momentum is a cost-robust candidate positive' to 'the recorded candidate evidence is an artifact of a price-level signal, and a docstring-faithful momentum implementation shows no REGIME_STABLE positive edge at any cost level (0/30 cells)'. The cost-robustness question is therefore answered negatively for this universe, this horizon, and this single corrected construction, and the momentum frontier cell is invalidated rather than qualified. What remains open is whether any other momentum construction produces an edge, which requires the signal repair recorded below.
